newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish treasury plans more Euro issues this year.
newsitem.headline: Turkish treasury plans more Euro issues this year.

text.p: The Turkish treasury is planning to raise more funds in the international borrowing market after a one-billion-mark deal last week despite continued political uncertainty, officials said.
"There are some offers for new issues in yen, French franc, Swiss franc, Italian lire and Dutch guilder. We are examining the offers," a treasury official told Reuters.
He did not give an exact date for the next issue.
Turkey set a one-billion mark, five-year Eurobond issue at a coupon of 7.25 percent and spread of 250 basis points last week.
But some bankers say deals in other currencies may not attract high demand amid increased political uncertainty, citing expatriate Turkish funds in Germany partly for the success of the mark deal.

Turkey has raised $1.35 billion through four deals so far this year -- last week's mark issue, a five-year $400 million issue in May, a five-year 300 billion lire deal in February and a seven-year 500 million mark issue in January.
It is planning to raise at least $2 billion in the international borrowing market in 1997.

"Despite all the negative political factors at home, the treasury is still able to borrow abroad successfully," the official said, referring to months of government crisis, aggravated by the ruling coalition's recent move to seek snap elections.

Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, who has been under intense pressure from the secularist army to crack down on religious activism, is planning to handover premiership to his coalition partner Tansu Ciller this month.
"I think our success in foreign borrowing will urge the rating agencies to revise our credit rating," the official said.
Turkey, with a foreign debt stock of $79.8 billion at end-1997, has a B rating from Standard and Poor's and B1 from Moody's.
"Pakistan's foreign currency reserves can only meet 2.5-weeks of imports. But it has the same rating with Turkey. This is unjust," the official said.

Turkey's total reserves stood at $25.6 billion on May 16 -- including the central bank's $16.9 billion of foreign currency and $1.3 billion of gold reserves. Its monthly imports are presently running at around $3.5 billion.
Bankers say Turkey should continue to borrow abroad to meet its foreign debt servicing and rely less on costly domestic borrowing markets.
According to figures obtained by Reuters the treasury will repay about $4.5 billion of external debt in the next seven months.
